text:
maria: quick update from the admission tuning run I kicked off this morning — going to paste highlights and a tiny repro. TL;DR: KV-aware proportional admit + adaptive token-budget cuts median latency and cancels a lot of soft queuing, but we see tail spikes when we hit a kernel handoff on 16k sequences.

kevin: nice, can you summarize numbers? p95/p99 changes?

maria: baseline (fixed token budget 256): p50 14ms, p95 120ms, p99 320ms.
proportional admit + adaptive budget: p50 11ms, p95 92ms, p99 350ms (regression on p99).

sanjay: p99 going up while p95 goes down screams rare kernel switch or batch misassembly. got flamegraphs?

maria: added perf summary from the worker that hit the worst tail. paste: 
```
profile: worker-37 (rtx-a100)
hotspots: kernel_select: 42% -> switched from int8-vec to fp16-conv at seq=16384
batch_assembly: 18%
kv_lookup: 12% (misses spiked to 34% for that window)
kv_cache_evict: 6%
context_copy: 5%
```

alice: interesting — so KV misses rise around the same time as kernel switch. could be prefetch window too small and we force a large batch that triggers a different kernel path.

maria: yep. hypothesis: proportional admit uses KV-hit fraction to scale token budget per-request, which normally avoids big batches, but when a burst contains many cold sessions we end up assembling a big multi-request batch -> triggers kernel selection for long sequences -> heavy tail.

kevin: can you share the admit config you used?

maria: config snippet below. note: `token_budget_base` is 256, `budget_scale_by_kv_hit` is linear here.
```
admit:
  mode: proportional
  token_budget_base: 256
  budget_scale_by_kv_hit: 1.5  # multiplier when kv_hit==1
  min_budget: 64
  max_budget: 2048
  reject_strategy: probabilistic_reject # probability ~ 1 - kv_hit
  backpressure_window_ms: 80
```

kevin: I think `max_budget: 2048` is too high for kernel stability. If a few cold requests coalesce you jump kernel branch. Maybe clamp max by observed batch sequence distribution.

sanjay: or make kernel-aware budget clamp: query runtime for kernel threshold (e.g., sequence sum threshold) and ensure admit doesn't create batches exceeding threshold. We already expose `kernel_hint` in the batcher. Could tune controller to prefer smaller batch when kernel_hint indicates fragility.

maria: good idea. I prototyped `kernel_guard: true` which enforces a soft cap: if estimated batch_seq_len > kernel_switch_point then reduce admit probability by 0.6. Results: p99 dropped to 210ms but p95 bumped to 110ms. tradeoff but safer.

alice: can you paste the quick repro command so infra can run the simulated burst?

maria: run in perf-sim mode: `./perf_sim --workload=kv_cold_burst --users=1200 --ramp=5s --duration=60s --admit-config=exp1.yaml --batcher-state=kernel_hint_on`

infra-bot: deployment note: perf_sim started on perf-node-12 at 1764504560, logs -> s3://redwood-perf/1764509999/run1.log

kevin: next steps I propose: 1) lower max_budget to 1024 and add kernel_guard threshold 2) add a small randomized jitter to admit decisions to avoid lockstep coalescing 3) collect KV-miss timelines per-batch to debug prefetch misses

maria: agreed. also adding a quick revert plan: if p99 > 300ms for 5m we auto-disable proportional scaling and fall back to fixed_budget.

sanjay: small implementation note: make kernel_switch_point available via /debug/kernels so controller can query cheaply. also need a cheap estimator for batch_seq_len before enqueue (sum of headroom estimate).

alice: I'll own the alerting change and the automatic fallback toggle. putting a quick playbook in case it trips: `playbook/admit-fallback.md` -> short runbook to revert to fixed-budget and roll out kernel_guard.

maria: will run a batch with: `max_budget=1024`, `kernel_guard=true`, `jitter=0.05`. will post new numbers in ~90m. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: sounds good. one more ask — can we log a single sample of raw batch composition (req ids, seq lens, kv_hit flags) for any batches that trigger kernel swap? even a tiny sample will help root cause.

maria: added `debug.sample_on_kernel_swap = 1` to config. sampling logs will be in the perf bucket.

infra-bot: perf job completed: status=ok, run_id=1764509999-1, artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/1764509999/run1.log

maria: new numbers after clamp/jitter/kernel_guard: p50 12ms, p95 98ms, p99 205ms. KV-miss windows reduced by ~40%. leaving experiment running for a few hours.

kevin: nice improvement. can we schedule a quick sync tomorrow to decide whether to keep proportional admit as default or restrict to non-peak hours?

maria: yes. added a follow-up calendar invite for tomorrow 10:30 PT.

sanjay: adding a note — long-term we should couple admit policy with the batcher's kernel selection predictor, not heuristics. open an RFC?

maria: will draft RFC after we stabilize the tuning. thanks everyone.
